box: Site-wide double-tap hazard: every game tap-transitions by calling stage.replaceChildren(), and each game's result screen appended its own <a href="/games/"> INTO #stage, so the new screen could place a navigation target at the coordinate the finger had just used and a double-tap navigated the group off their round mid-game (first confirmed in daily-fortune by docs/verification/evidence/34/12 + scripts/daily-fortune-double-tap-probe.mjs). Chosen mechanism is blast-radius reduction by construction, not a coordinate guard: #stage contains no navigation target at all, and the page's crawlable /games/ link becomes static chrome rendered by the layout. Three claims measured separately, because they fail for different reasons. Claim 0 (the mechanism, a set we own and can make empty): after every tap-driven transition in every game, #stage contains zero a[href]. Claim 1 (the harm): no point of the control the finger just used resolves via document.elementFromPoint to an element with an a[href] ancestor inside #stage. Claim 2 (an assumption the approach fork inferred but never measured): that same point never lands inside nav.game-next.
method: scripts/no-nav-in-stage-probe.mjs (committed) driven by scripts/driver.mjs against real headless Chrome 151.0.7922.138 (--headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --remote-debugging-port=9222) over a real build served with `npx serve dist/ -l 4321`. Two full runs of the same committed harness: one against the UNFIXED build (calibration) and one against the fixed build, nothing else changed. Per game, in one CDP tab: nav to /game/<id>/ FIRST, then session.setWidth(320,900), then wipe storage on-origin, then seed localStorage 'watduang:roster' with 8 long Thai names (the same roster as the daily-fortune double-tap probe), then reload so PlayerSetup's loadRoster() picks it up (browser-verification.md trap 4). The round is started through the REAL #start-round button after clicking all 8 roster checkboxes -- not by dispatching watduang:start directly, which leaves the setup panel on screen and makes every y coordinate below it a layout no player ever sees (the first attempt at this walk did exactly that and was discarded). Detector calibrated both ways per game before any tap is measured (trap 2): before the start the setup panel is visible AND #stage has 0 children; after it the panel is hidden AND #stage has children; innerWidth is read back as 320 each time. A walk that does not flip both halves, or that produces fewer transitions than its per-game minimum, or that reports a missing control, is scored FAIL as unusable rather than PASS. Each transition samples THREE points of the tapped control -- centre, top edge, bottom edge at centre-x -- because a real finger taps anywhere inside the control and centre-only sampling under-measures the hazard; each point is re-read with document.elementFromPoint on the screen that replaced it. Transitions walked: daily-fortune chip->result and #df-again->ask; siamsi #ss-start + 8x(#ss-draw, #ss-pass) + #ss-again (18); pick-loser #pl-pick->result and #pl-again->idle; short-stick every stick/#ss-pass tap until the short stick ends the round, then #ss-again (14 this run -- the short stick's turn is random, so the count varies); timebomb #tb-start->ticking, then the real timer-driven detonation with the finger's last position on #tb-pass (fuse waited 42401ms pre-fix, 36384ms post-fix -- the boom is not tap-driven, so this is the honest analogue, not a tap), then #tb-again->idle; love-match chip(first) in-place pick, chip(last)->result, #lm-again->pick. Also recorded per transition: the count of a[href] inside #stage, and the vertical gap between the tapped control's bottom and the top of the first in-stage anchor -- a negative gap means the anchor sits inside the box the finger just touched. Raw run JSONs were written to this session's scratchpad and are NOT committed; every number below is copied from them and every one is reproducible by running the committed harness the same way.

The six game files (in-stage hub anchor removed) and src/layouts/GameLayout.astro (static /games/ link added above #stage) are the exact change under test; the untracked file is the harness that measured it. The pre-fix half of this capture was run before any of those edits existed, at the same HEAD.
verdict: Claim 0 PROVEN and independently calibrated (red 6/6 pre-fix, green 6/6 post-fix). Claim 1 as measured by THIS harness's 3-point centre-x sampling was informative pre-fix (red 2/6, real calibration) but is ENTAILED by claim 0 once the fix is applied — #stage holding zero a[href] makes any in-stage-anchor hit structurally impossible, so claim 1's post-fix green is not independent corroboration, it is a restatement of claim 0. REFUTED as a general claim by scripts/gamenav-again-grid-probe.mjs and scripts/gamenav-start-grid-probe.mjs, which grid-scan the full control box instead of 3 centre-x points: post-fix, siamsi's and pick-loser's own GameNav anchors ARE reachable by real tap coordinates outside #stage (see refutingWholeBoxScans below). Claim 2 REFUTED (unchanged from original capture).
noTapCoordinateResolvesToAnyAnchorAnywhe: Refuted for GameNav anchors OUTSIDE #stage, reached by grid-scanning the whole control box rather than 3 centre-x points. Still true for anchors INSIDE #stage post-fix (that part is claim 0, proven).
postTransitionHitNeverLandsOnALinkInside: Refuted at wider sampling. The original 3-centre-x-point sampling never hit a link inside nav.game-next (only its <ul>/<h3> chrome), but scripts/gamenav-again-grid-probe.mjs's full-box grid scan shows the '#ss-again'/'#lm-again' button box itself overlaps GameNav <a href> links at roster 7-8 with long names — 25/60 sampled points in siamsi/love-match resolve to /game/pick-loser/, /game/short-stick/, /game/daily-fortune/, or /game/love-match/.

latentDefectNotTriggered.finding: scripts/no-nav-in-stage-probe.mjs computes inViewport at its line ~69 and records it at ~78, but no read of it feeds walkUsable (~219-230) or the pass/fail scoring (~254-256). A control positioned below ~900px (this harness's fixed viewport height) would make document.elementFromPoint return null at every sampled point, and stageAnchorCount/inStageAnchorHits would read 0 not because the mechanism holds but because nothing was actually hit-tested -- a vacuous PASS. This did NOT fire in any run captured here; it is a defect found by reading the code, not by a measurement going wrong.

note: The fix is the reason claim 0 is the primary check and claim 1 is not. Pre-fix, all six games shipped an a[href] inside #stage (claim 0 red six times) but the double-tap only actually LANDED on it in two of them, and the two were decided by pixels: -26px inside the tapped chip in daily-fortune, -4px inside the tapped stick in short-stick, against +28px (timebomb), +61px (pick-loser), +208px (love-match) and +339px (siamsi) of clearance. Those gaps are a function of Thai copy length x roster size x layout engine, and short-stick's -4px is produced by a randomly chosen short-stick turn, so which games are 'safe' changes between runs of the same build. A guard written against the coordinate would therefore have to enumerate a set nobody owns; emptying #stage of navigation targets is a set we own, which is why the post-fix green on claims 0 and 1 holds for reasons that do not depend on any of those numbers. What this capture does NOT cover: one roster size (8 names) and one viewport (320x900); one tap per control per screen (the first stick, the last chip) rather than every control; keyboard/form submit paths (daily-fortune's #df-go); real iOS WebKit hit-testing; and nav.game-next, which is page chrome locked by ADR-0013 and was not touched -- claim 2 is REFUTED and stays open as a separate finding, because the block IS reachable at a post-transition tap coordinate in siamsi and love-match, even though only its non-link chrome was hit here. Re-trigger this walk on any change to the games' render* functions, to #stage's position or styling, to GameLayout.astro's order above #stage, or to GameNav/nav.game-next's placement.
